main_body: A 4x3-tile farm ground patch: a golden crop or wheat field on top, a green grass fringe, then tilled brown soil furrows with grass tufts
top_band: none: this is a flat ground patch, not a standing object. The scan shows mixed crop dots (rows 0-14), then a grass strip (rows 16-19), then soil (rows 20+)
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the object-contract checks (top band, front face, opening) do not apply. The piece is a top-down ground surface made of crop rows, grass and furrowed soil. It stands up nothing, shows no receding side faces, and is not an elevation of any object. Terrain tiles are meant to be flat, so I pass it.

style.evidence: Each material has several steps: soil has dark brown, mid brown and light clod tones, grass has 3-4 greens, and the crop has cream, yellow, olive and ochre. The dark edges are tinted brown (0% neutral), so the outline is a material tone, not a black sticker line. Texture comes from crop speckle, soil grain and grass tufts, with 0% flat-fill coverage. Median colours per tile is 13, which is below the grass reference (26) but well above the paving reference (7) and above Beodeul's typical ~10. Total distinct colours (23) is much lower than the grass reference's 80, but the piece is a small, deliberately limited-palette patch, and it would not look thinner or flatter than the references when placed beside them.
